newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian government to review Iran credit line.
newsitem.headline: Australian government to review Iran credit line.

text.p: Australia's foreign minister said on Tuesday cabinet would discuss the future of a A$950 million (US$737 million) line of credit to Iran after a court linked the Islamic state to terrorism.

Foreign Minister Alexander Downer told reporters Canberra's response to the German court decision would be discussed during a cabinet meeting later on Tuesday. Australia has already withdrawn its ambassador to Iran.
Before entering the cabinet meeting, Downer was asked by reporters whether the credit facility to Iran was "on the line".
"That's an issue we've been discussing with the Iranians for quite some time," Downer said.

"Beyond that, I'm not going to get into speculation about different things we could do because I think it's important there's a reasonably well-coordinated international approach to the issue," he said.
Australia recalled its ambassador to Iran, Stuart Hume, after a German court last week ruled Tehran had ordered the 1992 murders of Kurdish activists in Berlin.
Downer has said Australia would consider a further response after studying the detail of the court ruling and consulting other governments.
